extracted.subtask_description: Practical, evidence-focused guidance for physicians on clinical observation, field collection of biological specimens, and topical therapeutics (notably ichthyol), together with technical specifications for related medical apparatus. Emphasizes acting on observed etiology, respectful scientific exchange, and procedural details for diagnosis and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize practical clinical evidence over taxonomic debate
rubrics_metrics.description: “Is it not that the mushroom poisoned the child? Next comes the nomenclature... Would the physicians feel justified to sit down and wait till the whole crowd of naturalists were satisfied... I trow not; they would warn the family...” — act on the clinical fact (cause and treatment) rather than waiting for perfect taxonomic nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confronted with a clinical emergency (e.g., poisoning, suspected malarial exposure), physicians should treat and warn based on the demonstrated etiology and best available evidence rather than delaying action pending resolution of scientific taxonomy or nomenclatural disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give respectful hearing and kindly review to colleagues presenting new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “If he asks us to look over his evidence, do so in a kindly spirit, and not open the denunciations of bar room vocabularies upon the presenter... we should all be receptive, but careful in our assimilation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novel claims courteously and on their merits. Avoid ad hominem denunciation; if a colleague presents evidence, examine it respectfully even if it challenges prevailing views. This is a professional duty when new findings may have practical importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit ignorance when outside your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: “If the subject is one about which we know nothing, we had better say so when asked our opinion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about limits of personal knowledge; defer judgment or refer when outside one’s specialty rather than offering uninformed opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional acceptance of a theory until better demonstration appears
rubrics_metrics.description: “So long as no one presents a better history of the etiology of intermittent fever by facts and observations, your theory must stand.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a provisional stance: accept working hypotheses supported by the best available observations until superseded by stronger evidence. This applies especially to etiologic claims with practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field collection and specimen-preservation methods for detecting 'ague' (malarial) plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical collection techniques are described: finding films from ash piles or pond holes, examining bog moss drip, searching soil about waterworks and pond edges, and examining patient sputa and excretions for plants; using a wet bandage wrapped around a slide to keep delicate algal specimens in condition for later examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attempting to detect microscopic environmental organisms (e.g., 'ague plants'), sample diverse microhabitats (pond holes, bog moss, ash piles, incrustations). Preserve fragile films by keeping slides moist (e.g., wrap with a wet bandage) until microscopy. Instruct lay collectors in simple collection technique and re-examine at intervals. Use macroscopical and microscopical inspection (e.g., solar microscope projections) to confirm identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ichthyol: therapeutic indications, efficacy hierarchy, and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ichthyol is described as a resolvent and a soother of pain and itching; useful in psoriasis (inferior to chrysarobin for P. inveterata), locally useful in rheumatic affections, acne, and as a parasiticide, with especially remarkable effects in various eczemas based on treatment of thirty cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ichthyol for moist circumscribed eczemas, intensely itching papular eczemas, infantile moist eczemas, and certain psoriasis and rheumatic local conditions. Expect variable efficacy (e.g., less effective than chrysarobin for some psoriasis). Use clinical judgment and monitoring; note that the author cautions against very widespread application pending better knowledge of internal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ichthyol dosing, formulation, and application protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended practical regimen: begin with a moderately strong preparation and progressively reduce strength. Strengths may range from 5% up to 40–50% or undiluted; for moist eczema use weaker preparations (20–30% decreased to 10%); for papular eczema use stronger (50% reduced to 20%); hands usually require stronger application than face; children require weaker applications than adults. Example formula for obstinate hand eczema: R. Lithargyri 10.0; coq.c. aceti, 30.0; ad reman. 20.0; adde olei olivar., adipis, aa 10.0; ichthyol 10.0, M. ft. ung.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor concentration to lesion type, anatomic site, and patient age; start stronger if clinically justified and taper as condition improves. Mix ichthyol with vaseline, lard, or oil as vehicle. Monitor for local irritation and systemic effects; exercise caution in widespread use until internal effects are better known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ichthyol chemical/compatibility notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ichthyol has a vaseline-like consistence, partly soluble in alcohol and ether, and is advantageously in intimate and stable union compared to ordinary sulphur preparations; it can be combined with lead and mercury preparations without decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate ichthyol ointments/emulsions using compatible vehicles (vaseline, oils) and note its relative stability; it may be safely combined with certain lead and mercury topical agents where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autopsy table design and functional specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Design features specified: top of thick, heavy cast glass concave toward the strainer (about eight feet long, two feet six inches wide) with a central opening to receive a strainer allowing fluids to pass to a waste pipe; a large strainer with downward draught passing through a flue connected above the water seal to the boiler-house chimney to carry offensive odors away; a ground-swinging base enabling rotation; hot and cold water cocks plumbing with a swing/ball joint under the base and a hose routed under the plate glass top for washing; design intended to avoid soiling the floor and to provide amphitheater viewing for juries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing an autopsy table prioritize: easy fluid drainage and containment (concave glass top with central strainer and waste plumbing), odor control (venting through flue to chimney above trap), mobility/rotation of the table (ground-swinging attachment), integrated hot/cold water with flexible delivery (ball joint and hose), and spectator viewing (central placement with surrounding amphitheater). Follow stated dimensions and practical attachments where appropriate to institutional needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and experimental findings for assessing the excitant property of oats ('avenine')
rubrics_metrics.description: The pericarp of oats contains an alcohol-soluble nitrogenized substance ('avenine') capable of exciting motor cells. All cultivated varieties elaborate it in varying degrees depending on variety and place of cultivation. Less than 0.9% of air-dried oats is insufficient to affect horses; crushing/grinding weakens the excitant; isolated principle acts more promptly; total duration approximated as one hour per kilogramme of oats ingested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To assess excitant action: chemically isolate and quantify the principle (determination of amount is the sure basis), account for varietal and cultivation-site variation (white varieties often less than dark), recognize processing effects (crushing/grinding reduces potency), and relate dose to expected duration (approx. 1 hour per kg). Use controlled electrophysiological measures of excitability before and after feeding in animal models where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filarial disease hypothesis and methodological caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Manson's propositions: he does not favor diurnal intermittent reproduction as explanation for filarial periodicity; hypothesizes that a parent filaria may abort and expel ova that act as emboli lodging in lymphatic glands producing stasis and hypertrophy, leading to elephantiasis, chyluria, etc.; death of the parent filaria in an afferent lymphatic may give rise to abscess. These conclusions are based on observations in a small number of cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use careful anatomic observation and case reports to formulate hypotheses about parasite-related pathology, but be cautious in generalizing from limited cases. Consider embryo size and lymphatic passage when proposing mechanisms. Seek further observational and experimental evidence before definitive causal claims.
